title: Has anyone tried Google’s TimesFM 3.0? Is it actually useful, or just hype?
author: mehulsharma01
selftext:
I recently came across TimesFM 3.0, Google’s open-weight time-series forecasting model, and wanted to know how well it performs in real-world use.

Has anyone here actually experimented with it? I’m particularly interested in:

\- How accurate is it on real-world datasets compared with traditional forecasting methods?

\- Can it handle multivariate time-series forecasting effectively, or are there significant limitations?

\- What are its practical use cases? Is it useful for stock market analysis, demand forecasting, business metrics, or anomaly detection?

\- How does it perform compared with models such as XGBoost, LightGBM, Chronos, Moirai, and other time-series foundation models?

\- Is it worth using in a personal project, or is it mostly hype around foundation models?

I’m interested in actual benchmarks, practical experiences, and limitations, rather than just theoretical capabilities.

If you have used TimesFM 3.0 or any alternatives, I’d appreciate your insights. Which model would you recommend exploring first for serious time-series forecasting projects?

comments.author: Emotional-Breath-838
comments.body:
My experiment will be to plug TimesFM forecasts into LightGBM alongside domain-specific technical indicators like volume, ATR, order flow, etc. to make directional decisions. 

If I have any luck, I’ll report back.

replies.body: Got completely derailed. I'll see if I can get back on track.

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: Foundation models forecast the series, not the edge. Plugging TimesFM output into LightGBM with order flow is the only sane use, the raw forecast alone is hype. Benchmarks look great until you add costs and slippage.
